sub_scenario.family: travel recovery physiology versus high-stakes scheduling
sub_scenario.one_line: touring stage manager: sign only with buffers or a named deputy

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the rigging checklist and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The tour itinerary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Overnight bus runs before travel days or dark days cost nothing.
Recovery-buffered overnights are free.
Free and routine on every tour.
Someone new shadowed me in the production office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the load-in calls into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My one logged near-miss, a rigging checklist item skipped, happened at a load-in that started eleven hours after an overnight bus run; my incident notes tie it to exactly that spacing.
The near-miss has a documented spacing signature.
Signed by me in the incident log.
Long load-ins on full rest are my favorite days of the job.
The work itself is not the hazard.
Never was.
I archived last cycle's notes on the tour itinerary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The union safety bulletin flags fatigue-compressed load-ins as the top rigging risk factor industry-wide.
Your log matches the industry data.
Matches it uncomfortably well.
A vendor call about the rigging checklist ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the production office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the load-in calls.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the tour itinerary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The festival offer routes three overnight jumps directly into morning load-ins across the leg; the routing sheet shows all three inside the spacing my log flags.
Three scheduled repetitions of the near-miss setup.
Three, on one routing sheet.
I sketched next week's plan for the load-in calls before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the rigging checklist updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Rigging sign-off on this festival cannot be delegated under their insurance terms unless a named deputy is contracted in advance.
The mitigation has a contractual path.
A path that must be written in now or never.
The tour promoter says every crew chief on the circuit runs these routings without complaint.
Everyone-does-it framing.
Framing my incident log declines to join.
I closed the week by updating the production office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The festival leg contract needs my answer. What do I require in it before signing?
